title: Case H — 1:1:2 building with a floor point source
summary: Isolated 1:1:2 building with an ethylene point source on the floor behind it: velocity (split-fibre hot wire) and concentration (hydrocarbon analyser) at 876 points.

configuration.U_H_note: the workbook's uH; the readme and the data paper state 3.23 m/s; the workbook's free-stream reference U0 is 5.279 m/s
configuration.source: 4 mm hole in the floor 0.25 H = 0.05 m behind the leeward face at (0.05, 0, 0); ethylene (C2H4), 100 %, 350 cc/min = 5.83e-6 m3/s
configuration.reference_concentration: c0 = cgas q / (UH H^2) = 45.18 ppm (45.2 in the paper); concentration_ratio = C / c0
configuration.instrument: velocity: constant-temperature anemometer (DANTEC 90C10) with a split-fibre probe (55R55, 55R56, 55R57), 1000 Hz, 120 s; concentration: high-speed total hydrocarbon analyser, 1000 Hz, 120 s
configuration.tunnel: Eiffel-type boundary-layer wind tunnel, Tokyo Polytechnic University, Atsugi (1.0 m high, 1.2 m wide)
configuration.scale_note: model scale; the source states no model:full-scale ratio; Eddy3D solves it at 1:100

frame.origin: the centre of the building's leeward face on the ground plane
frame.x: +x streamwise (the wind blows toward +x); the building spans x in [-0.1, 0]; points at x = -0.2 ... 0.4 m
frame.y: +y lateral; the building spans y in [-0.05, 0.05]; the z = 1/16 H plane covers y in [-0.2, 0.2]
frame.z: +z up; roof at z = 0.2 m; points at z = 0.01 ... 0.3 m
frame.lateral_sign_applied: -1 for point numbers 1-220 (the vertical-plane sheet of the workbook), +1 elsewhere

inflow_fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 2H on the workbook's 17-point approach profile (x = -0.493 m)
inflow_fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published by AIJ

fit.method: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 2H on the workbook's 17-point approach profile (x = -0.493 m)
fit.note: derived during cleaning, not published by AIJ

benchmark_data.note: the measured profile and the fit of it are the benchmark's data as cleaned here; everything under `recommended` is a choice

recommended.status: RECOMMENDED by this repository (not part of the benchmark): a log-law inlet fitted to the case's own approach-flow file, with k and epsilon from the standard neutral ABL relations. Any inlet may be submitted; say which in submission.yaml
recommended.profile: U(z) = u*/kappa ln((z + z0)/z0); k = u*^2 / sqrt(Cmu); epsilon = u*^3 / (kappa (z + z0))
recommended.fit: log law, kappa = 0.41, least squares over z = 0.02 ... 2H on the workbook's 17-point approach profile (x = -0.493 m)
recommended.openfoam: atmBoundaryLayerInletVelocity / atmBoundaryLayerInletK / atmBoundaryLayerInletEpsilon with Uref, Zref, z0 and d = 0; nutkAtmRoughWallFunction with the same z0 on the ground: cases/{id}/inflow_openfoam.txt holds them

flow_direction.meaning: +x is along the wind at WD = 0: flowDir (1 0 0); another WD rotates it about +z by the case's rotation sense (frame.wind_direction_rotation)

inflow.domain: the extents, blockage and cell sizes of Eddy3D's domains are not in its snapshots and are not stated here; mesh.cells and the scale are, where the snapshot has them

probes.columns_meaning: the key columns of a scored file (point_id with config, campaign, instrument, run and wind_direction_deg as the case has them), x, y, z in m (case frame), and scored_as: the families the row is scored in (vector, k, thermistor_bracket, concentration, theta, joined by +)

scoring.U_ref_meaning: U_H, the approach speed at the building height H = 0.2 m

scored_as.vector: U, V, W and the speed |U| against the split-fibre, LDV or hot-wire components (velocity.U, velocity.V, velocity.W, speed)
scored_as.thermistor_bracket: a mean scalar speed (thermistor, cup or sonic anemometer) against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar)

scoring.conventions: velocities and the speed over U_ref, k over U_ref^2 (Cases E, F and G publish ratios already); U, V, W, |U| and the thermistor bracket scored as signed velocities (FAC2's ratio keeps the sign; hit rate D = 0.25, W = 0.05); k by the plain definitions (D = 0.25 only); a thermistor, cup or sonic reading (a mean scalar speed) scored against |U| (vs.vector) and sqrt(|U|^2 + 2k) (vs.scalar), the two ends of its bracket; c* = C/c0 with one detection limit per case, 1e-3 of the largest measured value; theta = (T_floor - T)/(T_floor - T_H) scored like a positive velocity. The same conventions score the served Eddy3D results (docs/validation/method.md).
scoring.tool: uv run python validation/score_submissions.py <folder>, from a checkout of the repository (pyproject.toml)

metric_meaning.MeanObserved: mean of the measured, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.MeanPredicted: mean of the modelled, normalised quantity
metric_meaning.Fb: fractional bias, 2 (mean_obs - mean_pred) / (mean_obs + mean_pred); positive = model low
metric_meaning.Fac2: fraction of points within a factor of two (harsh near zero for sign-changing V and W)
metric_meaning.HitRate: fraction of points within D = 0.25 relative or W = 0.05 U_H absolute
metric_meaning.GeometricPairs: pairs with both values positive (used for Mg/Vg)
metric_meaning.null: a metric that is undefined for the data (for example Mg and Vg when no pair has both values positive; Fb, Nmse and Nad of a signed velocity component of Case H or I whose observed and predicted means are not both positive)

known_issues: The table carries the legacy workbook's values (ratios at full precision x uH = 3.226 m/s), not RS_caseH.csv's: on the z/H = 1/2 and 1/4 planes (and in the approach profile) the CSV's U, V, W are the workbook ratios ROUNDED TO 0.01 before the scaling, a 0.032 m/s grid (+/-0.016 m/s).

One row per instrument and point: velocity rows (split fibre) and concentration rows (hydrocarbon analyser) with the same point_id (the CSV's No.). The velocity line is x = 0.40 m and the concentration line x = 0.38 m, so 50 points have no velocity and 50 no concentration (-999.9 in the CSV); none of them is inside the building.

V of the vertical-plane sheet (point numbers 1-220) is the exact negative of V at the same points in the horizontal-plane sheets (positive toward -y); it is multiplied by -1 so that V is positive toward +y everywhere, as in Cases A and D.
The y = 0, z = 0.1 line (13 locations) is in two sheets and appears twice in the table, as exact copies once V is flipped; they are not independent repeat measurements.

Concentration is the analyser's reading: upwind of the building (where the true value is zero) it is +/-0.1 ppm, and 97 of 826 values are negative (minimum -0.83 ppm). Log-based statistics (geometric mean, geometric variance) need a floor.
The published header misspells w_rms as 'w_rsm'; the workbook's inflow sheet labels z as 'mm' but holds metres.
The profile's uw and uv are published but the approach-flow table has no column for them.
